fields.name: problem
fields.value: Refund settlement takes 9 days on average

evidence.quote: Small-business sellers wait 9 days on average for marketplace refunds to settle.

fields.name: affected_users
fields.value: Small-business sellers and finance operations analysts

evidence.quote: Finance operations analysts handle the resulting disputes manually.

fields.name: evidence
fields.value: 41% of surveyed sellers paused restocking

evidence.quote: 41% of surveyed sellers said delayed refunds forced them to pause restocking.

fields.name: cost_of_inaction
fields.value: About 120 sellers lost per quarter

evidence.quote: we expect to keep losing roughly 120 sellers per quarter to competing marketplaces

fields.name: primary_metric
fields.value: Median refund settlement time

evidence.quote: The primary metric is median refund settlement time.

fields.name: baseline
fields.value: 9 days

evidence.quote: It is currently 9 days.

fields.name: target
fields.value: 2 days

evidence.quote: We will reduce it to 2 days.

fields.name: measurement_window
fields.value: 90 days after general availability

evidence.quote: Success is judged over the 90 days after general availability.

fields.name: guardrail_metric
fields.value: Dispute contact rate below 3%

evidence.quote: Dispute contact rate must not regress above 3%.
Cross-border refunds are explicitly out of scope for this release.

fields.name: primary_flow
fields.value: Authenticated seller requests an eligible refund and sees settlement status

evidence.quote: The primary flow starts when an authenticated seller opens an eligible order, requests a refund, and ends when the seller sees the settlement status.

fields.name: preconditions
fields.value: Seller owns the order, has permission, and requests no more than the captured amount

evidence.quote: The seller must own the order, have refund permission, and provide an amount no greater than the captured payment.

fields.name: requirements
value: Sellers can request a refund from the order detail screen
The system validates order eligibility before submitting
Refunds over 500 USD require manager approval

evidence.quote: Sellers can request a refund from the order detail screen.

fields.name: prioritisation
fields.value: Request and validation are must-have; manager approval is should-have

evidence.quote: The request and validation flows are must-have for launch, and manager approval is a should-have.

fields.name: decision_rules_and_precedence
fields.value: Eligibility rejection wins over approval; duplicates return the original result; otherwise use standard settlement

evidence.quote: If eligibility rejection and manager approval both apply, eligibility rejection wins; duplicate requests return the original result, and all other eligible requests use the standard settlement path.

fields.name: criteria
value: Eligible order settles within 2 business days
Ineligible order shows a rejection reason and creates no refund record

evidence.quote: A refund request on an eligible order settles within 2 business days.

fields.name: failure_and_boundary_criteria
value: Reject amounts above the captured payment
Reject duplicate requests without a second refund

evidence.quote: Requests without permission, above the captured amount, or submitted twice must be rejected without creating a second refund.

fields.name: requirement_coverage
fields.value: AC-1 maps request flow, AC-2 eligibility, and AC-3 permission, amount, duplicate, and approval boundaries

evidence.quote: AC-1 covers the must-have request flow, AC-2 covers eligibility validation, and AC-3 covers permission, amount, duplicate, and manager-approval boundaries.

fields.name: error_states
fields.value: Payment provider failure queues the request and shows a retry banner

evidence.quote: On payment provider failure the request is queued and the seller sees a retry banner.

fields.name: empty_or_edge_states
fields.value: Seller with no refunds sees an empty state

evidence.quote: A seller with no refunds sees an empty state explaining eligibility rules.

fields.name: transitional_or_degraded_states
fields.value: Loading during eligibility checks and resume from queued state after interruption

evidence.quote: While eligibility is checked the seller sees a loading state, and an interrupted request can be resumed from the queued state.

fields.name: supported_platforms
fields.value: Responsive web, iOS, and Android

evidence.quote: The supported platforms are responsive web, iOS, and Android; other channels are excluded from this release.

fields.name: accessibility_approach
fields.value: WCAG 2.1 AA with keyboard and screen-reader checks

evidence.quote: The web and mobile flows must meet WCAG 2.1 AA, keyboard-navigation, and screen-reader checks before launch.
We will log refund_requested, refund_settled, and refund_rejected events.

fields.name: metric_link
fields.value: Settlement time computed between refund_requested and refund_settled

evidence.quote: Median settlement time is computed from the interval between refund_requested and refund_settled.

fields.name: operational_signals
fields.value: Queue-depth dashboard and alert above 100 queued refunds

evidence.quote: Operations monitors settlement queue depth on a dashboard and receives an alert when queued refunds exceed 100.
This depends on the Payments platform team, the Ledger service, and our payout vendor.

fields.name: dependency_readiness
fields.value: Owned API, idempotency, and vendor interfaces have readiness checks; stale or unavailable vendor input queues on the legacy path

evidence.quote: Payments owns the refund API and must pass its availability check by build start; Ledger owns the idempotency endpoint and must pass duplicate-request tests by QA; the payout vendor must confirm its daily file interface before pilot, and if it is stale or unavailable, requests remain queued on the legacy path.

fields.name: constraints
fields.value: Vendor daily cut-off at 18:00 UTC

evidence.quote: Settlement cannot exceed the vendor daily cut-off of 18:00 UTC.

fields.name: data_handled
fields.value: Seller bank account identifiers and transaction records

evidence.quote: The flow handles seller bank account identifiers and transaction records.

fields.name: purpose_and_minimisation
fields.value: Existing bank token is needed only to route the refund; no new bank details are collected

evidence.quote: Bank identifiers are required only to route the refund; the flow stores the existing token rather than collecting new bank details.

fields.name: access_and_third_parties
fields.value: Finance Operations and Payments can access the token; payout vendor processes it

evidence.quote: Only Finance Operations and the Payments service can access the token; the payout vendor processes it under the existing data-processing agreement.

fields.name: review_status
fields.value: Privacy review requested and scheduled before build

evidence.quote: A privacy review has been requested and is scheduled before build starts.

fields.name: data_lifecycle
fields.value: Audit records retained 7 years; bank identifiers deleted after 30 days

evidence.quote: Transaction audit records are retained for 7 years, while bank account identifiers are deleted 30 days after settlement.

fields.name: rollout_mechanism
fields.value: Feature flag to 5% of sellers

evidence.quote: We will release behind the rapid_refund feature flag to 5% of sellers first.

fields.name: launch_and_stop_criteria
fields.value: Expand after 7 days at 2-day settlement and under 3% contacts; pause above queue depth 100 or 1% errors

evidence.quote: We expand after 7 days if median settlement is at most 2 days and dispute contacts stay below 3%; we pause if queue depth exceeds 100 or error rate exceeds 1%.

fields.name: rollback_plan
fields.value: Disable the flag to revert to the legacy refund path

evidence.quote: The flag can be disabled to revert all traffic to the legacy refund path.

fields.name: rollout_owner
fields.value: Maya Chen owns decisions and Payments on-call executes rollback

evidence.quote: Maya Chen owns rollout decisions and the Payments on-call lead can execute rollback.

fields.name: support_and_communications
fields.value: Support guide and seller notice; no sales or marketing campaign

evidence.quote: Support receives a troubleshooting guide before pilot launch; affected sellers receive an in-product notice, while sales and marketing need no launch campaign.

fields.name: rejection_reasons
value: Does not scale beyond 200 refunds per week

evidence.quote: That was rejected because it cannot meet a 2 day target.

fields.name: assumptions
value: At least 70% of delayed refunds qualify for the accelerated route
Sellers understand the existing settlement-status language

evidence.quote: We assume at least 70% of delayed refunds are eligible for the accelerated vendor route and that sellers understand the existing settlement-status language.

fields.name: validation
fields.value: Transaction-data analysis by Priya and seller research before design sign-off

evidence.quote: Priya Raman will validate route eligibility against August transaction data by 2026-09-27, and Design Research will test the status language with five sellers before design sign-off.

fields.name: service_expectations
fields.value: 40 refunds per second, p95 below 500 ms, queued recovery within 30 minutes

evidence.quote: The service must sustain 40 refunds per second, keep refund API p95 latency below 500 ms, and recover queued requests within 30 minutes after a provider outage.

fields.name: support_owner
fields.value: Payments on-call with Finance Operations escalation

evidence.quote: The Payments on-call team owns monitoring, first-line incident response, and escalation to Finance Operations.

fields.name: recovery_plan
fields.value: Runbook covers diagnosis, rollback, queue replay, and Ledger reconciliation

evidence.quote: The rapid-refund runbook covers queue diagnosis, feature-flag rollback, replay from the durable queue, and reconciliation against Ledger records.
